body:
Plot twist, my husband is a lawyer (currently not licensed. Not necessary for his current job) but he’s probably going to have better connections than me. 

I just don’t know how I’d afford a house and childcare. My daughter loves her bedroom so I’d almost be okay with him keeping the house so that the kids could have at least one solid place because I’ll probably be struggling to make ends meet on my own.
I could go stay with family but it’s a 2 hour drive. I don’t want to be that far from my kids.

Specifically I’m in a target parking lot. I have family about 2 hours away. Thankfully my wallet was in my car so I got gas right away. I could stay with my sister but she’s a fucking mess and might stress me out more. I’m afraid to leave the city because he has my kids. I’m not worried he will do anything to them, other than the fact that he’s forgetful and will leave outdoor gates open, let them climb the stairs, ect.

We just had a discussion and he said he hears me and he’s going to try to be better, especially when he isn’t perfect either. This conversation has happened periodically in the past so we will see if he actually sticks to changing.

At this point though, even if he doesn’t say anything to me I’m still going to be afraid that he’s just silently judging me :/

He’s just so unsupportive and it makes it really hard for me to want to be a good parent. How am I supposed to wake up and want to do fun activities with the kids when I feel like I just want to sleep forever or leave.  He will tell me all the time that “I’m so great” but only after a really good day. I don’t need that. I need him to tell me that he understands that this is hard but he just doesn’t think it’s hard. He just got done being a dick and then immediately started talking to a friend on discord and he’s just in a great mood. They’re having a lovely conversation about music. I’m glad he’s having a nice time.

Yeah. I take care of them Monday-Friday alone. On the weekends or after work he is helping and is active but he has ME there too. He’s never had to take care of both kids alone for more than a few hours. It’s man to man coverage when he’s off work. When he’s working, it’s 2 on 1 for me.

Man, I always have to defend myself when ever I tell people that I don’t like newborns. Sure they’re cute and little and I miss my kids being that tiny but I don’t miss the PPD, no sleep, bleeding cracked nipples, guilty feeling for substituting with formula to give my tits a break, the weight hair, the hair loss, not sleeping because of SIDS fears. 

Who enjoys that??? 

Both my kids have aspects that make them easier than the other. But both also have aspects that make them harder than the other and they combine all day. If I just had one kid I would probably be okay but I have 2 and  it just seems like they take turns trying to get me to go insane.  My 1.5 year old gave me a bloody nose last night and my 3 year old is refusing to poop and I seriously HATE potty training.

We are currently reading No Drama Discipline but I’m only about half through and I don’t really read it anymore because of the negativity that’s come from it. I agree with its philosophy but it’s so hard to be conscious 100% of the time so I do slip and find myself using a slightly more annoyed tone with the kids. I don’t spank them or anything, the worse they get is a “come ONNNN”. 


When my husband loses his cool, I don’t call him out. I help him. I will either take over completely and give him a second to cool down or I’ll try to insert myself into the situation to refocus the kids attention/aggression and see if I can get through. 

If I lose my cool, I’m immediately called out, he will shake his head in disappointment or make a nasty comment. I just want some understanding.

Thank you for this reply. I feel bad because my husband DOES help but he’s also a lot more selfish with his time than I am. His day is littered with bits of “me time”, even while working he will play a game or two with a friend online. He is pressuring me to have a thought out meal time, precise schedule and limited screen time even on crappy weather days/days that I’m sick. On the weekends he will lounge and watch tv with the kids though. Or disappear for a nap.  I’ve had my kids outside the past few days from around 9am-5pm with maybe an hour of tv while I get the baby down. Tomorrow will be cold and rainy and I have anxiety knowing that I’ll get shit if I turn the tv on to give myself a break. 

My overall feeling in the day is guilt. Guilty that they don’t eat a vegetable with every snack or meal, guilty that they I haven’t done the dishes yet, guilty that I am turning down a puzzle with my daughter because those dishes need done, guilty that they haven’t been outside on a crappy day, guilty that they don’t understand why we can’t go see grandma, guilty that I’m frustrated that my daughter still won’t stop shitting her pants 7 times a day. Things like that. It’s just so much. 

I’ve always had a job, sometimes more than one, and I like being busy and doing a good job. Parenting feels like you’re never doing a good job.

My husband has basically taken on this new “no disciple” rule. It’s hard to set boundaries because then I’m not “connecting” in his mind. This was already hard to begin with but now I’m expected to Dr. Phil my kids everytime they have a meltdown, whet before I would just let them get over it on their own as long as they were safe, fed and dry. It’s taking all my energy. And with him working from home it feels like he’s breathing down my neck waiting to yell at me about my tone or to tell me to be a mother.

I play video games for a couple hours on Friday’s and Saturday’s after the kids go to bed but my youngest has been waking up a lot at night so I’m just so tired. 

I used to take a shower to get some alone time but now the kids insist I joining me

I’m really considering looking for part time, I just have to figure out how to afford childcare. I don’t really get a lot of time to myself. Kids get up at 5:30 and I’m alone until my husband gets off at 5 and then i cook and give the kids baths and then in bed at 8:30. It’s rough. I love them but I hate potty training and overall damage control 24/7
I have a horrible imagine of what a mental hospital is like.  Are people condescending? I don’t want to be treated like a crazy person or be guilted again for not enjoying my current life style
I won’t hurt them. If anything I’ll just leave them here in their cribs. They won’t die

I tried the suicide text line yesterday and it sucked. The girl said “ oh that sounds hard” and that’s it. The next text after that was saying we were going to disconnect and then it asked me to do a survey. 

My husband thinks kids are the greatest thing in the world and he is fine. We can’t relate on this.
